requirement: Verify a JWT and require that its space-separated scope claim grants every needed scope, reporting all missing scopes at once.
skeleton: InsufficientScopeError holding the missing set, granted_scopes parsing and type-checking the claim, and require_scopes validating its arguments, decoding and comparing sets.
caption: Scope-based authorization on top of PyJWT. InsufficientScopeError carries the frozenset of missing scopes and its message is missing scopes: followed by them sorted and space-joined. granted_scopes(claims) reads the scope claim with an empty default, raises TypeError saying the scope claim must be a space-separated string when it is not a str, and returns frozenset(raw.split()), so extra whitespace is ignored and a prefix such as orders:readonly never grants orders:read. require_scopes(token, secret, *needed) raises ValueError saying at least one scope must be required when none are given, decodes with algorithms pinned to HS256 so jwt.InvalidSignatureError propagates, and raises InsufficientScopeError with every needed scope that is not granted. The fixture asserts that a token with orders:read and orders:write passes for both, that padded whitespace still grants users:read, that asking for three scopes with only orders:read reports orders:write and users:read in that message, that orders:readonly does not grant orders:read, that a token without scope grants nothing, that a list scope raises TypeError, that no needed scopes raises ValueError, and that a foreign signature raises jwt.InvalidSignatureError.

plan.intent: Authorize API calls by OAuth scope
constraints: Scopes are whitespace-separated tokens compared exactly, never by substring
Every needed scope must be granted, otherwise InsufficientScopeError reports all missing ones
A token without scope grants nothing
A non-string scope claim raises TypeError
Signature failures such as jwt.InvalidSignatureError propagate

rationale.teaches: Parse the scope claim into a set with str.split and check needed minus granted, so matching is exact and all-of.
rationale.why: Substring checks let orders:readonly satisfy orders:read and any-of checks let a single scope unlock every endpoint, and neither fails a happy-path test.

ops.docstring: Authorize a call from the space-separated scope claim of a verified JWT.

candidates.why_wrong: Scopes are split on commas, so a space-separated claim becomes one unusable scope.
Access is refused only when every scope is missing, so one granted scope unlocks the rest.
A list scope is stringified instead of rejected with TypeError.
A token without scope crashes with KeyError instead of being refused for missing scopes.
Scopes are matched by substring, so orders:readonly grants orders:read.
